questions.questionText: Huygens' principle states that every point on a wavefront acts as:
questions.solution: Each point on a wavefront is a source of secondary wavelets.

questions.questionText: In Young's double slit experiment fringe width is:
questions.solution: Fringe width beta = lambda*D/d.

questions.questionText: Constructive interference occurs when path difference is:
questions.solution: Constructive interference when path diff = n*lambda (integer multiples).

questions.questionText: Destructive interference occurs when path difference is:
questions.solution: Destructive when path diff = (2n+1)*lambda/2 (odd half wavelengths).

questions.questionText: Diffraction is more pronounced when:
questions.optionB: Slit width is comparable to wavelength
questions.solution: Diffraction is significant when obstacle/slit size is comparable to wavelength.

questions.questionText: In single slit diffraction the central maximum width is:
questions.solution: Central max width = 2*lambda*D/a (twice the width of other maxima).

questions.questionText: Polarization proves that light is:
questions.solution: Only transverse waves can be polarized.

questions.questionText: Brewster's angle is related to refractive index by:
questions.solution: Brewster's law: tan(iB) = n.

questions.questionText: In YDSE if slit separation is halved, fringe width:
questions.solution: beta = lambda*D/d. Halving d doubles beta.

questions.questionText: Coherent sources are those which have:
questions.optionB: Same frequency and constant phase difference
questions.solution: Coherent sources have same frequency and constant phase relationship.

questions.questionText: The resolving power of a microscope increases with:
questions.solution: Shorter wavelength gives better resolution (smaller limit).

questions.questionText: In YDSE using white light, the central fringe is:
questions.solution: At centre path diff = 0 for all wavelengths so all colours constructively interfere giving white.

questions.questionText: Malus's law states transmitted intensity through polaroid is:
questions.solution: Malus's law: I = I0*cos^2(theta).

questions.questionText: Fresnel distance is:
questions.solution: Fresnel distance zF = a^2/lambda.

questions.questionText: If YDSE is performed in water instead of air, fringe width:
questions.solution: In water lambda decreases (lambda/n) so fringe width decreases.

questions.questionText: The phenomenon of bending of light around obstacles is:
questions.solution: Diffraction is bending of light around edges of obstacles.

questions.questionText: Intensity at a point in interference pattern where phase diff is phi:
questions.solution: For equal intensity sources I = 4I0 cos^2(phi/2).

questions.questionText: Diffraction pattern of single slit has first minimum at:
questions.solution: First minimum: a sin(theta) = lambda.

questions.questionText: Angular width of central maximum in single slit diffraction:
questions.solution: Angular width = 2*lambda/a.

questions.questionText: Two polaroids with axes at 90 degrees transmit:
questions.solution: cos^2(90) = 0, so no light passes through crossed polaroids.

questions.questionText: Wavefront of a point source at large distance is:
questions.solution: At large distance from point source wavefronts are approximately plane.

questions.questionText: Interference and diffraction both require:
questions.solution: Both phenomena need coherent light for observable patterns.

questions.questionText: In YDSE if D is doubled keeping d and lambda same, fringe width:
questions.solution: beta = lambda*D/d. Doubling D doubles fringe width.

questions.questionText: Resolving power of telescope depends on:
questions.solution: Resolving power = D/(1.22*lambda), depends on objective diameter D.

questions.questionText: The phenomenon where light intensity varies between maxima and minima is:
questions.solution: Interference produces alternating bright and dark fringes.
